name: Argentina

findings.summary: A 2019 report said Huawei was Argentina's main 4G supplier: Movistar's mobile core fully Huawei, Huawei supplying 70% of Telecom's national network, plus Claro fibre/microwave and about a third of ARSAT's fibre backbone.
findings.analyst_inference: Article states its figures came from Huawei-linked sources and operators declined to comment; shares may be outdated after 2018-2024 vendor changes. Current 5G core vendors unverified.

findings.summary: Ericsson won a 4G RAN expansion and upgrade deal with Telefónica Argentina running to 2021, lifting its share of the operator's RAN to about 80% from an even split with Huawei.
findings.analyst_inference: Partial displacement of Huawei in RAN by commercial choice, not a ban, so not coded as a reversal. Pole third (Sweden). Core network not covered.

findings.summary: Nokia was named sole supplier for the first phase of Claro Argentina's 5G radio access rollout in the largest cities, using AirScale baseband and IPAA+ antennas.
findings.analyst_inference: RAN only; contract value undisclosed. TeleSemana corroboration based on its search-result headline, not fetched. Pole third (Finland). Audit 2026-10-22: no longer corroborated, because a second source was seen only as a search-result headline.

findings.summary: Milei's government announced Stargate Argentina: a planned Patagonian AI data centre of up to 500 MW and up to US$25 billion by Sur Energy, with OpenAI signing a letter of intent. By May 2026 no RIGI application had been filed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: Sur Energy is described as Argentine-US owned with no ownership split, so controller jurisdiction is unclear. Stalled per May 2026 reporting but no official cancellation or pause found, so not coded as a reversal. DCD source seen in search results only. Audit 2026-10-22: no longer corroborated, because a second source was seen only as a search-result headline.

findings.summary: Under the Stargate Argentina letter of intent, OpenAI would buy the planned data centre's computing capacity; financing was to come from investment funds rather than OpenAI.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded to models layer as the OpenAI offtake side of the bundle; no government adoption of OpenAI models for public services found. Audit 2026-10-22: BA Times (May 2026) reports no public progress since October 2025.

findings.summary: Neuquén cooperative CALF announced an expanded strategic partnership with Huawei to grow its connectivity network; a US embassy warning of visa restrictions followed, and CALF said it would not change plans solely because of it.
findings.analyst_inference: Preliminary agreements only; definitive contracts unsigned as of August 2026. US visa pressure is not a reversal unless CALF withdraws. Sub-state actor, not a national decision.

findings.summary: CALF and Huawei held talks, under preliminary agreements, to develop a regional data centre in Neuquén near Vaca Muerta and supply equipment; definitive contracts were not yet signed.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller of the planned facility is unclear (CALF would likely own it, Huawei supply it); coded prc on the vendor because the article frames it as Huawei's project. Value undisclosed. Audit 2026-10-22: US visa warnings to CALF managers escalated in August 2026 and may decide the deal.

findings.summary: Jujuy province contracted ZTE for a public-security system of about 600 cameras, monitoring centres, a 911 centre and fibre links for 310 sites, financed by a US$24m BBVA Hong Kong credit line with a national sovereign guarantee.
findings.analyst_inference: Values differ: DPL News cites US$30m, Aduana News a US$24m credit line; announced value recorded from DPL News. Operational status today not verified. Audit 2026-10-22: Value is the US$24m credit line given by the cited source, not US$30m.

findings.local_actor: Municipality of Magdalena (Buenos Aires province); VIMOX S.R.L.
findings.summary: A trade-press case study described a Hikvision IP camera surveillance network covering Magdalena's towns, integrated by VIMOX and linked to a central monitoring office, already operating.
findings.analyst_inference: Tiered S4: reads as vendor-supplied case study. Old, small-scale deployment; current status unknown.

findings.local_actor: Servicio Meteorológico Nacional; Secretaría de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología
findings.summary: Clementina XXI, a state supercomputer at the weather service bought in 2022 for US$4.9m with CAF financing, uses 296 Intel Ponte Vecchio GPUs; it reached full operation in 2025 and was opened to firms for AI work in 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us on the accelerator vendor; system is state-owned and integrator Lenovo is PRC-headquartered. Value is the 2022 purchase price, not an audited figure. Small compared with commercial AI clusters.

power.null_reason: no AI-specific power deal confirmed; Stargate energy partners (Central Puerto, Genneia) mentioned only in passing and unverified

corrections.note: Migrated to spec v0.2 (scale, reversal_reason, still_current, builder/financier, base model, opened flags; corroboration recomputed on opened sources) and audit corrections applied.

research_gaps: Current 5G RAN/core vendors for Telecom Argentina (Personal) and Movistar; Huawei's present share after 2018-2024 changes.
Has CALF signed definitive contracts with Huawei, or withdrawn under US visa pressure (a reversal if so)?
Is Stargate Argentina dead, revived under 'Super RIGI', or relocated? Sur Energy ownership split.
Neuquén Espacio Lejano station (PLA-linked deep-space ground station): Argentine delegation inspected it in September 2026 per BA Times headline; not an AI-stack layer, not coded, outcome unread.
No national Huawei/ZTE ban or exclusion under Milei found; 2023 5G auction reportedly did not exclude Huawei (unverified).
Status of Jujuy ZTE system and any other provincial safe-city deals (Hikvision/Dahua).
Government adoption of foreign frontier models or a sovereign Spanish-language model not searched in depth.
